newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shrs fall in kerb, Chidambaram yet to speak.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shrs fall in kerb, Chidambaram yet to speak.

text.p: Bombay shares slipped slightly in kerb deals on Monday as punters sold on news the lower house of parliament approved a part of India's 1996/97 budget, traders said.
But parliamentary officials in New Delhi said the finance bill would be put to a vote before the scheduled adjournment of parliament on Friday.
They said Finance Minister P. Chidambaram was scheduled to speak on Tuesday.
Officials said the appropriations section of the budget was passed on Monday but tax proposals were still to be approved.
Reliance fell to 207 rupees from its official close of 208.50, TISCO slipped to 187 rupees from 190.75 and State Bank of India dropped to 276.50 rupees from 278.50.
Traders said punters sold on rumours Finance Minister P. Chidambaram was unlikely to reply to an ongoing budget debate on tax proposals.
